name: aligned-card-grid
title: Aligned card grid
description: Cards that line up inside: every card is a subgrid, so titles, bodies and footers share rows and the buttons sit on one baseline.
docs: Build a grid with AlignedCardGrid and put AlignedCardGrid.Card in it: each card is a subgrid with one row for every part you list in rows (media, title, body and footer by default), so the parts of cards side by side share their rows. Write the parts of a card in the order of rows: Media (with an optional ratio such as 4/3; the picture runs to the edge of the card), Title (an h3, or the level you pass with as), Body and Footer, or Part with a name for a row of your own (rows={["title", "body", "price", "features", "footer"]} and <AlignedCardGrid.Part name="price">). A card may leave a part out and its neighbours keep their rows; list only the rows that exist, so a row nobody uses takes no room. The card itself has 20px of room under its last part, so a card without a footer still ends clear of its text (pass pb-0 to a card whose last part is a picture). minCardWidth is the narrowest a card may get (16rem by default) and the grid fits as many columns as the width allows, stretching the cards when a row is short; gap is sm, md, lg or any length. Where subgrid is missing the cards are flex columns of equal height with the footer pushed to the bottom. The cards use the Card surface. For a list, give the grid role="list" and each card role="listitem".
